questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select option 'No substitution required'.**

The interview __was broadcast__ on the same day he was sworn in as President.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 2'** i.e.** 'No substitution required'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the verb "**broadcast"** in the passive voice correctly, which is "was broadcast." This is the correct form for referring to an event in the passive voice in the past.
 
• **"Broadcast" **is both the past and present form of the verb, unlike other verbs that typically end in -ed for their past forms. Thus, **"was broadcast" **is correct.
 
• The context of the sentence does not require a perfect tense ("had broadcast") because it clearly states that the interview was broadcast on the same day he was sworn in. There is no need to emphasize the sequence of events.
 
• The sentence is **grammatically correct **and conveys the message clearly and effectively without any ambiguity.
 
• Using **"broadcast" **in this construction is correct and aligns with standard English usage for referring to events transmitted on television, radio, or other broadcasting mediums.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **No substitution required.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1, "had broadcast,"** introduces the past perfect tense, which is unnecessary here since the action's timing relative to another event is already clear.
 
• **Option 3, "was broadcasted,"** is a common mistake. "Broadcasted" as the past form is less preferred; the standard past simple and past participle form is "broadcast."
 
• **Option 4, "broadcast"** without any auxiliary verb would shift the sentence to the present tense or suggest an imperative mood, which does not fit the context of a past event being described.

questions.question: Which comoponent of blood ﬁghts against germs that enter human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**White blood cells.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• **WBCs **fight against the germs that enter the human body.
 
• Also known as **leukocytes**** **are a part of the immune system of our body.
 
• These are produced in Bone Marrow and have an average lifetime of 3-4 days.
 
• WBCs produces antibodies and ingest foreign material to fight infection.
 
• These are of three types lymphocytes, granulocytes, and monocytes.
 
 
• **Lymphocytes**: These are further classified as T and B cells.
 
 
• **T cells **recognize the infected cells.
 
• **B cells **secrete antibodies.
 
 
 
• **Granulocytes**: These help the body to get rid of large pathogens like protozoa. Granulocytes are further divided into neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils.
 
• **Monocytes**: These are also known as Scavenger cells. Destroys the pathogens at the site of infection and clears debris.
 
 

 
 

 **Component of Blood**
 **Characteristics**
 
 

 RBC
 
 
 
• Also known as Erythrocytes.
 
• Produced in: Spleen, Liver and Bone Marrow.
 
• Average lifetime: 120 days.
 
• It contains hemoglobin that carries oxygen to all parts of the body.
 
• Carry carbon dioxide to the lungs.
 
 
 
 

 Platelets
 
 
 
• Also known as Thrombocytes.
 
• Produced in: Bone marrow.
 
• Average lifetime: 3-7 days.
 
• ​Help in blood clotting.
